title_en: Build a Singleton base class with one instance per subclass
spec_html_en: Write class Singleton implementing __new__ so that each concrete subclass gets its own single shared instance: _instances must be a dict keyed by the class itself, so two different subclasses never share the same instance, but two calls to the same subclass always return the same one.
test:
class Logger(Singleton):
    pass

class Cache(Singleton):
    pass

def test_same_subclass_returns_same_instance():
    a = Logger()
    b = Logger()
    assert a is b, 'two calls to the same subclass must return the same instance'

def test_different_subclasses_get_different_instances():
    logger = Logger()
    cache = Cache()
    assert logger is not cache, 'different subclasses of Singleton must not share the same instance'

def test_each_subclass_keeps_its_own_state():
    logger = Logger()
    logger.name = 'app-logger'
    same_logger = Logger()
    assert same_logger.name == 'app-logger', 'the shared instance for a subclass must keep its state across references'
